name: Fresh water (river, lake)
notes: River and lake margins: willow and alder on banks, cattail/reed/bulrush emergents in the shallows, water lilies and floating plants on still water, and submerged pondweed/water milfoil below. Drawn on temperate Eurasia and North America; underwater species flagged. Warm, still, shallow, sunny water is the niche of the sacred lotus (on Earth native to Asia and northern Australia, not the Amazon), the giant Victoria water lily (the Amazon) and the water lilies of the Nile and the Maya lowlands; none is in the catalogue now, and under design §CS each land's warm ponds would get their own community.

canopy.name: River birch

growth.juvenile_note: Seed shed in late spring germinates at once on wet, freshly exposed river sand and silt. Epigeal: two tiny round cotyledons, then small toothed rhombic leaves. A fast slender whip that soon forks or sprouts from the base, so young trees are often clumps of two or three stems already showing curling salmon-pink bark.
growth.source: USDA Silvics of North America vol. 2 (Grelen, river birch): the only birch whose seed ripens in late spring (May-June); seed germinates without dormancy on moist alluvium; fast growth, very intolerant of shade, short-lived for a tree; first seed age and lifespan estimated from that account

ground.name: Liverwort

growth.juvenile_note: A spore grows into a short green filament, then a tiny flat plate; gemmae (lens-shaped buds splashed out of cups on the thallus) grow straight into little two-lobed thalli. The plant is a flat, forking, ribbon-like green thallus up to 10 cm long and 2 cm wide with a dark midline, pale pores and little cup-shaped gemma cups; stalked umbrella-like sex organs rise from mature patches.
growth.source: Shimamura 2016 Plant Cell Physiol. 'Marchantia polymorpha: taxonomy, phylogeny and morphology of a model system' (gemma to sexual maturity in ~1-2 months in culture); Wikipedia (thalli to 10 x 2 cm; rapid colonist that can carpet burned ground); field timings and lifespan estimated

repro.note: spores by wind and water; no flowers; needs a wet film to reproduce, so spread reads moisture not pollinators

ground.source: Wet ground, stream banks and burns worldwide; flat green scales with umbrella stalks; the first plant back after fire on wet ground. Kew POWO.

ground.name: Stream lichen

growth.juvenile_note: Starts as a tiny brown scale on a stream rock that is under water part of the year. It grows outward into rounded, leathery, overlapping lobes 0.5-2 cm across, each fixed by a central holdfast; grey-brown and stiff when dry, soft and bright green when wet, with the pores of its sunken fruit bodies showing as dark dots.
growth.source: Brodo, Sharnoff & Sharnoff, Lichens of North America (Dermatocarpon luridum: lobes 0.5-2 cm, brown dry and green wet, on rocks in streams and along lake shores, often submerged); British Lichen Society; growth rate and ages estimated from other umbilicate lichens

repro.note: spores from sunken fruit bodies; no flowers; lobes break and lodge downstream

ground.source: Dermatocarpon luridum, brookside stippleback, Holarctic; leathery leafy lichen of rocks in and beside streams and on lake shores that spend part of the year under water — Brodo, Lichens of North America / British Lichen Society

leaf.notes: overlapping rounded leathery lobes, grey-brown to red-brown when dry, bright grass-green when wet, finely dotted with the dark pores of sunken fruit bodies

appearance.seasonal: brown when dry, green when wet
appearance.silhouette: brown-green leafy lichen patches on wet stream rocks
appearance.refs: Brodo et al. Lichens of North America; British Lichen Society

ground.name: Taro

growth.juvenile_note: Almost always grows from a corm or side cormel (true seed is rare): a pointed shoot unrolls into a small rosette of long-stalked leaves. Blades are heart- to arrow-shaped and peltate (stalk joined inside the blade), velvety and water-repellent; each new leaf is bigger until the clump of 'elephant ear' leaves on 1 m stalks is reached in 5-7 months, with cormels budding around the base.
growth.source: Wikipedia Taro (leaves to 40 x 25 cm on 0.8-1.2 m petioles; matures 6-12 months after planting on dry land, 12-15 months in wetland, early cultivars 5-7 months; propagated by corms and cormels; perennial); PROSEA/FAO taro accounts (sprouting in 2-4 weeks, flowering rare, grows in partial shade)

repro.note: giant herbs, not trees: each stem grows in a season, fruits or flowers once and dies, replaced by suckers from the clump — fast growth stages, visible in weeks

ground.source: SE Asia; wet fields and stream banks everywhere in the tropics. The staple root of the wet tropics; camp folk plant it in water; camp-follower. Kew POWO.

ground.name: Bucephalandra motleyana

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds are flicked out of the cup-like lower spathe by raindrops (splash-cup) and lodge in moss or cracks on wet stream rocks. The seedling is a tiny rosette of 2-3 small elliptic leaves gripping the rock with roots; a creeping rhizome then adds leaves and branches into a dense mat over the stone.
growth.source: Wikipedia Bucephalandra (rheophytes forming mats on rocks in Bornean forest streams; splash-cup seed dispersal); Kew POWO; aquarium grower growth rates (2-3 leaves a week in fast forms, 1 per 2 weeks in slow); timings estimated.

repro.note: beetle-pollinated; seeds float downstream; needs flowing water

ground.source: Bornean rainforest streams on rock; the widespread species; purple-tinged. Kew POWO.
